'''Choe Thae-bok''' ({{Korean|hangul=최태복}}; 1 December 1930 – 20 January 2024) was a North Korean politician. He was a member of the Politburo and the Secretariat of the [[Workers' Party of Korea]], and was chairman (speaker) of the [[Supreme People's Assembly]] for nearly 21 years, from 1998 to 2019. He was considered an advisor to [[Kim Jong Il]],<ref name ="nklw">[http://nkleadershipwatch.wordpress.com/leadership-biographies/choe-tae-pok-choe-thae-bok/ Choe T'ae-pok (Choe Thae Bok)], North Korea Leadership Watch.</ref>{{Unreliable source?|reason=See reliable sources list on [[WP:KO/RS]]|date=May 2025}} as well as a popular member of the core leadership.<ref name="nklw"/> He spoke fluent English, German and Russian in addition to Korean.

==Biography==
Choe was born in [[Namp'o]], [[South Pyongan Province]], on 1 December 1930.<ref>[http://www.kcna.co.jp/item/2010/201009/news29/20100929-07ee.html "Profiles of Presidium and Members of Political Bureau"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402092716/http://www.kcna.co.jp/item/2010/201009/news29/20100929-07ee.html |date=2 April 2015 }}, KCNA, 29 September 2010.</ref> He was one of the first to study at the [[Mangyongdae Revolutionary School]]; he later studied chemistry at the [[Kim Il Sung University]], and completed his studies in Leipzig (then in East Germany) and Moscow. After his return to North Korea, he worked as a schoolteacher. In 1965 he worked at the [[Hamhung]] Chemical Engineering College as director of research of the Hamhung Branch of the Chemical Research Institute under the National Academy of Sciences, and as dean of the college in 1968. In 1972 he began working as the section chief at the WPK Education Department, becoming its vice-director in 1976.

Starting from the late 1970s, when he was appointed faculty dean and later president of the [[Kim Chaek University of Technology]], Choe took a more prominent role in the [[Politics of North Korea|country's politics]]. In the 1980s he served as chairman of the Education Commission from 1980 and Minister of Higher Education from 1981. In those capacities he expanded cultural exchanges with other countries and programs to let North Korean students study abroad. Choe was first elected as a deputy to the [[Supreme People's Assembly]] in 1982. In the same year, he led an SPA delegation to France. This was the first time he led North Korean delegations on official visits, which later included journeys to the Soviet Union, East Germany, China, and Bulgaria in 1984&ndash;1985.

In 1984, he was appointed as an alternate member of the [[6th Central Committee of the Workers' Party of Korea|6th Central Committee]], then full member and member of the [[6th Secretariat of the Workers' Party of Korea|6th Secretariat]] in 1986, and [[6th Politburo of the Workers' Party of Korea|6th Politburo]] member in 1990. As secretary, Choe was put in charge of education, science and cultural exchanges. Choe was elected chairman of the 10th, 11th and 12th SPAs, a role that increased his involvement in foreign affairs. He also served as chairman of the Korean Committee for Solidarity with the World People from 1993 to 1998. Despite his purported reformist views, he was reputedly close to Kim Jong Il's sister [[Kim Kyong-hui]] and Vice-President [[Yang Hyong-sop]] of the SPA Presidium.<ref name="nklw"/>

On 6 January 2007, at a mass rally in Pyongyang, he gave a speech praising the North Korean government for building nuclear weapons.<ref name="6 Jan 2007">{{cite news|title=Usher in a great heyday of Songun Korea full of confidence in victory|newspaper=[[The Pyongyang Times]]|date=6 January 2007|page=1}}</ref> On 19 October 2012, he met [[Zandaakhuu Enkhbold]], the Mongolian parliamentary speaker, and the two countries "agreed on the future possibilities of bilateral trade and cooperation in the fields of information technology and human exchanges."<ref name="port dec 2012">{{cite web|title=Rise in popularity of Rajin Port|url=http://ifes.kyungnam.ac.kr/eng/FRM/FRM_0101V.aspx?code=FRM121130_0001|publisher=Institute for Far Eastern Studies (IFES)|accessdate=5 December 2012|date=30 November 2012|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150313051049/http://ifes.kyungnam.ac.kr/eng/FRM/FRM_0101V.aspx?code=FRM121130_0001|archivedate=13 March 2015}}</ref> ''[[Choson Sinbo]]'', a pro-Pyongyang newspaper in Japan, said that Mongolia was interested in exporting coal, copper, gold, and uranium through [[Rason|Rajin]] [[Port]] because it was "costly to rely on Chinese and Russian railway systems."<ref name="port dec 2012"/> In October 2017 he retired as vice chairman of the WPK.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nkleadershipwatch.org/2018/03/22/spa-will-meet-on-april-11/|title=SPA Will Meet on April 11 &#124; North Korea Leadership Watch}}</ref> He was then replaced as speaker of the SPA at the new legislature's first session in April 2019.

Choe died from a heart attack on 20 January 2024 in [[Pyongyang]], at the age of 93. His death was announced by ''[[Rodong Sinmun]]'', and [[KCNA]] reported that [[Kim Jong Un]] visited his grave.<ref>[http://www.rodong.rep.kp/ko/index.php?OEAyMDI0LTAxLTIxLU4wMDRAMkBAQDFAMw== 최태복동지의 서거에 대한 부고] {{in lang|ko}}</ref>
